chunks.pt: Embeddings: The Geometry of Meaning

chunks.pt: Embeddings: The Geometry of Meaning

chunks.pt: Embeddings: The Geometry of Meaning

chunks.pt: Embeddings: The Geometry of Meaning

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: the states it has to regulate.

chunks.x: Initialization: Controlled Chaos — We previously

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: We previously mentioned initializing weights

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: “randomly.” But “random” is a dangerous word in

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: engineering.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: If we pick weights from a Uniform Distribution

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: between -1000 and 1000, the signal will explode

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: towards infinity (NaN).

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: If we pick them between -0.0001 and 0.0001, the

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: signal will vanish to zero.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: we saw in the Statistics part.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: initialization: pick random numbers from a

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: Gaussian Bell Curve whose width is set by the

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: size of the layer.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: He initialization, designed for ReLU, uses

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: variance 2/nᵢnputs:

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: Xavier initialization, designed for tanh and

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: sigmoid, also takes the number of outputs into

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: account, typically with variance

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: 2/(nᵢnputs+nₒutputs).

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: This ensures that the “energy” (variance) of the

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: data stays constant as it flows through the

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: network, preventing the math from breaking before

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: Matrices as Parallel Processing — A single neuron

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: A single neuron computes y = ax + b: one input,

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: one weight, one output.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: But a Transformer with dₘₒdeₗ = 4096 processes

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: 4096 numbers simultaneously at every step.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: The bridge between these two scales is the matrix.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: Instead of computing one neuron at a time, we

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: pack all inputs into a vector x and all weights

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: into a matrix W.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: The entire layer's computation becomes:

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: This single line represents thousands of

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: individual multiplications and additions, all

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: happening in parallel.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: Every row of W is a separate “neuron” with its

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: own set of weights.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: Every row of W receives the same input x.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: The matrix multiplication Wx computes the dot

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: product of every row with x simultaneously.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: This is why GPUs are so effective for deep

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: learning: they are designed to perform matrix

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: multiplications in hardware, processing thousands

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: of operations per clock cycle.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: A modern GPU can execute a 4096 × 4096 matrix

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: times a 4096-dimensional vector, over 16 million

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: individual multiplications, in a single operation.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: Without this parallelization, training a model

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: like GPT-4 would be computationally impossible.

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: So when you see h = Attention(Q, K, V), remember

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: that every letter in that equation is a matrix,

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: and every operation is a batch of thousands of

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: parallel arithmetic operations, each one as

chunks.pt: Smallest possible neural network
chunks.x: simple as the single neuron y = ax + b.

chunks.x: ## Dataset Splits: Why You Can't Test on the Same

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Data You Trained On

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: A fundamental rule in machine learning: never

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: evaluate your model on data it has already seen.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: This is why datasets are split into separate

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Training Set (typically 70-80%): Used to adjust

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: the model's weights.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: The model sees this data and learns from it.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Validation Set (typically 10-15%): Used to tune

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: hyperparameters (learning rate, architecture

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: choices) and detect overfitting.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: The model does not learn from this data, but it

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: influences human decisions about the model.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Test Set (typically 10-15%): Held back until the

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Used only once to report final performance.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: If you ever use the test set to make decisions,

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: you are cheating, and your reported accuracy will

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: be optimistic.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Why three sets?

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: If you tune hyperparameters on the validation

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: set, information about the validation set “leaks”

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: into your model choices.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: You need a third, completely untouched set to get

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: an honest measure of generalization.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: In small-data regimes (e.g., medical imaging with

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: only hundreds of samples), k-fold

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: cross-validation is used instead, where the data

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: is repeatedly split into k folds, and each fold

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: takes a turn as the test set.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: A model is only as good as the data it is trained

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: If the training data contains historical biases,

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: the model will learn and amplify them.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: This is not a bug in the math, it is a feature of

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: the statistical learning process: the model

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: faithfully reproduces the patterns it observes.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Historical Bias: The data reflects existing

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: societal inequalities.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: A hiring model trained on historical hiring data

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: will learn the gender and racial biases present

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: in past decisions.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Representation Bias: Certain groups are

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: under-represented in the dataset.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: A facial recognition system trained mostly on

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: light-skinned faces will perform poorly on

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: dark-skinned faces, as documented by Joy

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Buolamwini, Timnit Gebru in 2018.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Measurement Bias: The features used to represent

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: the data are noisy or systematically wrong for

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: certain groups.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Label Bias: Human annotators introduce their own

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: subjective judgments into the training labels.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: The technical consequence: Bias in data leads to

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: systematically different performance across

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: subgroups.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: The model's overall accuracy may look good, but

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: disaggregated by demographic group, it can reveal

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: dramatic disparities.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Detecting and mitigating these biases is an

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: active area of research in fairness in machine

chunks.x: The theoretical framework underlying much of

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: supervised learning was formalized by Vladimir

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Vapnik in the 1960s–1990s.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: His Statistical Learning Theory asks a

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: fundamental question: given a finite set of

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: training examples, how can we bound the error on

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: unseen data?

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: VC-Dimension (Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension): A

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: measure of a model's capacity or complexity.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: A model with higher VC-dimension can fit more

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: complex patterns but risks overfitting.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: The VC-dimension of a linear classifier in d

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: dimensions is d + 1; for a neural network, it can

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: be proportional to the number of parameters.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Structural Risk Minimization (SRM): Instead of

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: minimizing only the training error (Empirical

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Risk Minimization), SRM minimizes a combination

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: of training error and model complexity.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: This is the theoretical justification for

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: regularization techniques like weight decay and

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: The Bias-Variance Tradeoff: Models with low

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: capacity (high bias) underfit; models with high

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: capacity (low bias, but high variance in

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: predictions across different training sets)

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: overfit. The optimal model balances both.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: A significant step toward reconciling this

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: framework with practice: Philipp Petersen, Jakob

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: covering number of the network class (Ch.\ 14)

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: and show that in the overparameterized regime,

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: small weights (as initialization provides) make

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: the relevant function class Lipschitz-bounded

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: independently of the parameter count — so the

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: bound no longer degrades as you add parameters

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Every Normal Distribution is fully defined by

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: just two numbers: μ (Mean): The center of the

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: bell curve.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: σ (Standard Deviation): The width/spread of the

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Step 2: Standardize with the Z-Score — To look up

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: To look up probabilities, we convert any value x

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: into a Z-score, which tells us how many standard

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: deviations x is from the mean:

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: This transforms any Normal Distribution into the

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Standard Normal Distribution N(0, 1), which has μ

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: = 0 and σ = 1.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: This is the key trick: instead of needing a

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: different table for every possible μ and σ, we

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: only ever need one table.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Why This Matters for AI: Batch Normalization, one

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: of the most important techniques in deep

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: learning, is essentially computing Z-scores for

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: every layer's activations during training.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: At each layer, the network computes:

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: This is the same standardization Pearson used in

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: his biometric work to make measurements on

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: different scales comparable.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Without it, the activations in deep networks tend

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: to drift toward extreme values (a problem called

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: internal covariate shift), causing gradients to

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: vanish or explode and training to stall.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: By standardizing activations back to μ = 0, σ = 1

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: at every layer, the network stays in a regime

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: where learning is stable and fast.

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: Layer Normalization, used in every Transformer

chunks.pt: Statistics I — Distributions and Inference
chunks.x: (including GPT), applies the same principle.
